name: Temporal Phase Coherence under Scheduler Jitter
research_question: Can individually stable timing/update modes become unstable or semantically divergent when scheduler jitter switches among them, and what timing receipts/robustness envelopes must FRANK/ClayCode expose?

hypotheses.claim: Per-mode correctness/stability is insufficient; switching among timing modes can amplify coupled state unless the schedule family itself is tested.
GWT/Hyperposition delay interventions should report a temporal robustness envelope over schedule/jitter classes, not only single fixed-delay points.
ClayCode likely needs executable time/deadline/epoch receipts in runtime/ABI semantics before any new language syntax is justified.

counterhypotheses: A single deterministic scheduler may make schedule-family robustness unnecessary for authoritative paths.
If all relevant coupled update operators share a common contraction/Lyapunov certificate, arbitrary switching may already be safe.
Some slow or derived state can tolerate jitter if it is excluded from consequential authority and causally tagged by epoch.

experiment.interpretation: Both fixed update operators are individually asymptotically stable by spectral radius, yet a legal alternating switch product has spectral radius >1 and strongly amplifies the state. This is a mechanism counterexample to inferring schedule-family safety from per-mode safety.
experiment.boundary: Synthetic linear mechanism only; not live FRANK evidence.

external_grounding.source: Lincoln & Cervin, Jitterbug: A Tool for Analysis of Real-Time Control Performance, IEEE CDC 2002
external_grounding.support: Delay, sampling jitter, output jitter, lost samples and period overruns can be analyzed as implementation timing effects on control performance.

external_grounding.source: Cervin et al., Jitterbug and TrueTime: Analysis Tools for Real-Time Control Systems, 2002
external_grounding.support: Real-time control analysis/co-simulation explicitly couples task scheduling and process dynamics.
Linux real-time behavior requires explicit scheduling/preemption/locking treatment; realtime execution is an implementation property, not implied by ordinary correctness.

branch_implications.gwt: Extend delay_changed counterfactuals into schedule-family/jitter-envelope sweeps bound to episode IDs and state epochs.
branch_implications.hyperposition: Treat delay/timescale metadata as an active switching surface; measure robustness under alternating/multi-rate coupling, not only static delay values.
branch_implications.claycode: Route first to CC-WP-09-CONCURRENCY-MEMORY and runtime receipts: logical_time, observed_latency, deadline/budget, source_epoch, target_epoch, schedule_class, nondeterminism receipt. No syntax change absent executable counterexample.
branch_implications.harness: Add deterministic schedule-fuzzing and worst-case alternating-pattern tests while model outputs are frozen; record semantic divergence, GWT winner changes, re-entry validity and recovery.
